title: On the Divine Names and The Mystical Theology
author: Pseudo-Dionysius (Rolt trans)
description: Dionysius the Areopagite on the Divine Names and the Mystical Theology, translated with an introduction by C. E. Rolt (SPCK, 1920). The author, writing around 500 CE under the name of St Paul's Athenian convert, fused Christian theology with the Neoplatonism of Proclus, and his works became authoritative in both Eastern and Western Christianity. The Divine Names examines the names given to God in scripture, such as Good, Light, Beauty, Love, Being, Life, Wisdom, Power, Peace and One, interpreting them as the processions of the divine into creation while affirming that God transcends all names. The brief Mystical Theology teaches the way of negation: ascending beyond all affirmations and denials into the 'divine darkness' of unknowing where God is met beyond knowledge. Rolt's long introduction relates the works to Neoplatonism and later mysticism. These texts founded Christian apophatic theology and shaped Eriugena, Aquinas, Eckhart, the Cloud of Unknowing and Cusanus.
